title: Ashwin and Dravid Reunite in Dublin. Europe's First ICC-Sanctioned T20 League Just Got Its Star Power.
excerpt: The European T20 Premier League held its inaugural draft on Thursday, with Ashwin captaining Dravid's franchise and Maxwell, Steve Waugh and Jonty Rhodes all owning teams across Ireland, Scotland and the Netherlands.
body:
The European T20 Premier League (ETPL) is a sentence no one expected to write in world cricket. But on Thursday, in a draft room that doubled as a statement of intent, Ravichandran Ashwin, Glenn Maxwell, Jonty Rhodes and Steve Waugh sat side by side as franchise principals of a league designed to bring ICC-sanctioned T20 cricket to Ireland, Scotland and the Netherlands.

The draft confirmed squad compositions for the league's six city-based teams — Dublin Guardians, Amsterdam Flames, Rotterdam Dockers, Belfast Irish Wolves, Edinburgh Castle Rockers and Glasgow Cosmics — ahead of its inaugural season running from August 26 to September 20 across all three countries.

## Ashwin's Dublin Chapter

The headline act is the 39-year-old Ashwin, who will captain and mentor the Dublin Guardians, a franchise owned by former India captain Rahul Dravid. It is the latest chapter in one of Indian cricket's most enduring professional bonds — Dravid coached Ashwin through a T20 World Cup triumph in March 2026, and now trusts him with the cricketing soul of his European venture.



"I think freedom is very important for people to be able to run a cricket team on the field," Ashwin said after the draft. "Rahul has been very clear that he doesn't want to be involved as much in cricketing decisions. Which is why I am at the centre of it."

Ashwin, who retired from the IPL after the 2025 season with 537 Test wickets to his name — second only to Anil Kumble among Indians — is currently playing for the San Francisco Unicorns in Major League Cricket in the United States. The ETPL adds a third continent to his franchise portfolio.



> **""Rahul has been very clear that he doesn't want to be involved as much in cricketing decisions."**


## A Star-Studded Ownership Table

The ETPL's ownership group reads like a who's who of world cricket. Beyond Dravid in Dublin, Steve Waugh co-owns the Amsterdam Flames, where Mitchell Marsh and Steven Smith are marquee signings alongside Dutch internationals Scott Edwards and Bas de Leede. Glenn Maxwell captains and co-owns the Belfast Irish Wolves. Faf du Plessis, Heinrich Klaasen and Jonty Rhodes co-own the Rotterdam Dockers alongside Bollywood star John Abraham, while the league itself counts Abhishek Bachchan among its investors.


![Glenn Maxwell — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3d/Glen_Maxwell_2026_%28cropped%29.jpg)


Glasgow have signed Lungi Ngidi, Keshav Maharaj, Duan Jansen and Finn Allen, with Matthew Hayden serving as co-owner and head coach. Mitchell Santner will captain Edinburgh alongside Trent Boult, with Kyle Mills and Nathan McCullum among the ownership group.

## Why This Matters for Cricket

The ETPL is jointly backed by Cricket Ireland, Cricket Scotland and the Royal Dutch Cricket Association, making it Europe's first ICC-sanctioned multi-country franchise T20 competition. It is a direct attempt to replicate the development model that the IPL pioneered in India and MLC has accelerated in the United States.

Maxwell, speaking to the media after the draft, drew a direct parallel. "You've only got to look at a team like the US," he said. "Their growth is probably on the back of the success of the MLC and how that tournament has helped grow cricket in that part of the world."


![Jonty Rhodes — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9b/JONTY_RHODES.jpg)


The league's deeper ambition is structural: young players from Ireland, Scotland and the Netherlands sharing dressing rooms, coaching sessions and competitive pressure with some of the game's biggest names. "There's some world-class names throughout the league, and it's a hard competition not to pick up some tips that might help these players in their games," Maxwell said.

## The Diaspora Angle

For NRIs across the UK, Ireland and Europe, the ETPL is the closest franchise cricket has ever come to their doorstep. Dublin, Belfast, Edinburgh and Glasgow are all cities with significant Indian and South Asian diaspora populations. The opportunity to watch Ashwin bowl in Dublin, Maxwell bat in Belfast, or Marsh smash sixes in Amsterdam — all within a weekend trip — is a first for cricket fans on the continent.

Ireland's own cricketing rise has been powered partly by diaspora contributions. Jai Moondra, born in India, played a starring role in Ireland's recent historic T20 series win over India. The ETPL hopes to formalise and accelerate that pipeline.

"Hopefully, the same thing will happen with the ETPL," Maxwell said. "It can happen quite fast… inspiring the next generation of cricketers."
